summary_html: Immediate state action to **protect a child in imminent danger**. Federal law (ASFA/IV-E) ties funding to court findings on **reasonable efforts**, and constitutional limits (due process, 4th/14th Amendments) constrain warrantless removals.
authority_html:
- **ASFA / SSA Title IV-E** — reasonable-efforts findings; permanency timelines  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal oversight of removal decision quality  
- **Constitutional constraints** — enforced via §1983 actions; due process & search/seizure jurisprudence (not listed in file but governs practice)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: K.D. v. County of Crow Wing
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court held that emergency removal of a child without a court order is constitutionally permitted when continued parental custody poses an imminent threat to the child's health or welfare, and affirmed summary judgment for the Minnesota county and officers.
key_cases.relevance: It is the governing Eighth Circuit rule, in a Minnesota case, for when protective custody may be taken without prior judicial authorization.
key_cases.quote: In cases in which continued parental custody poses an imminent threat to the child's health or welfare, emergency removal of children without a court order is constitutionally permitted.

key_cases.case_name: Heartland Academy Community Church v. Waddle
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed injunctive and declaratory relief, holding that the wholesale removal of boarding students on stale ex parte orders or with no order at all, absent exigent circumstances, violated the Fourth Amendment.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Eighth Circuit's leading statement that protective custody without a valid order requires probable cause or exigent circumstances.
key_cases.quote: Waddle effected the wholesale removal of HCA's boarding students with ex parte orders or no orders at all in the absence of exigent circumstances

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court held that a Minnesota county social worker's 72-hour protective hold of a student under an ex parte order was objectively reasonable and that the order was not so lacking in probable cause as to make reliance on it unreasonable, granting qualified immunity.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Eighth Circuit's application of the protective-custody standard to a Minnesota 72-hour hold under an ex parte order.
key_cases.quote: The ex parte order was not so lacking in indicia of probable cause as to render Diercks's reliance on it unreasonable.

key_cases.case_name: Mitchell v. Dakota County Social Services
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed dismissal of a Minnesota father's § 1983 claims, holding that a CHIPS petition filed two days after removal followed by a hearing within ten days supplied all the procedural process he was due.
key_cases.relevance: It fixes the post-removal hearing timeline that follows an emergency protective custody in Minnesota.
key_cases.quote: In child removal cases, the meaningful time and manner requirement means that the state must hold a hearing promptly after removal.

timeline_requirements.deadline: Except in a noncaregiver human trafficking assessment: immediately if sexual abuse or substantial child endangerment is alleged; within 5 calendar days for all other screened in reports
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified by statute; Minn. Stat. § 260E.20, subd. 2(b) sets the face-to-face contact deadline for the local welfare agency.
timeline_requirements.extension_grounds: Face-to-face contact on a report alleging sexual abuse or substantial child endangerment may be postponed for no more than five calendar days if the child is residing in a location confirmed to restrict contact with the alleged offender, or if the local welfare agency is pursuing a court order for the caregiver to produce the child for questioning under Minn. Stat. § 260E.22, subd. 5 (§ 260E.20, subd. 2(b)).

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified by statute; Minn. Stat. § 260E.24, subd. 1 requires the local welfare agency to conclude the assessment or investigation within 45 days.
timeline_requirements.extension_grounds: Only to complete a criminal investigation or to receive expert information requested within 45 days of receipt of the report (Minn. Stat. § 260E.24, subd. 1).
